revisions.old_description: A pet bites, chews, or pulls furniture or its upholstery with its mouth.
revisions.new_description: Alert when the pet is biting, chewing, or pulling on furniture. Biting and chewing involve the mouth, while pulling counts whether done with the mouth or paws. Resting at the same time still counts if any of biting, chewing, or pulling is happening.
revisions.note: After an initial missed detection, the furniture event definition was expanded to clarify biting, chewing, pulling with the mouth or paws, and concurrent resting. A visual rerun detected chewing at 0–10s. The remaining visual events, Safety Watch instructions, silent input, model and reasoning settings were unchanged. The original audio check was retained, so this clip combines separate inference runs and is excluded from aggregate latency.

The eating-at-bowl recording was excluded after the initial evaluation because obscured bowl contents prevented reliable annotation of eating versus drinking. Labels for the remaining clips were unchanged.

latency.note: Processing from an already-available window, including preparation; no live capture wait. Cleanup is separate. Clips combining checks from separate runs are excluded from the latency mean.

limitations: Small development set, not held-out evidence or a broad safety validation.
Revised development-set results: exclusions and prompt changes after initial results are listed in Revisions. No repeatability estimate.
Clip/event accuracy and false-positive counts are not alert-level false-alarm rates.
Safety Watch is scored as any visible danger, not hazard kind or identity accuracy.
Unavailable checks are excluded from classification accuracy and reported in processing coverage.
Only the original labeled source-time intervals are used; long-term absence and hotspot accuracy are not evaluated.
